newsitem.title: USA: MICH. UNEMPLOYMENT RATE FALLS TO 3.8 PCT IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: MICH. UNEMPLOYMENT RATE FALLS TO 3.8 PCT IN JULY.

text.p: Michigan's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate broke the 4 percent barrier for the first time in more than a quarter century, dropping to 3.8 percent in July, the state employment security agency reported Wednesday.

The seasonally adjusted rate had been 4 percent in June and was 4.9 percent a year ago, the department reported. The rate had not dropped below 4 percent since the agency began using the current calculation method in 1970.
Employment has grown by 109,000 jobs over the past year and 527,000 since July 1991, the agency reported.
The overall number of jobs in Michigan dropped 7,000 in July with somewhat larger losses than normal in the education sector, the agency reported.
Job gains were reported in motor vehicles, retail trade, transportation/communications/utilities and services sectors.
The national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 4.8 percent in July.
